Introduction

Pasadena is experiencing a significant shift toward electric vehicle adoption, and the city is actively supporting this transition through its utility provider, Pasadena Water and Power. As more residents and businesses in Pasadena make the switch to electric vehicles, the demand for qualified electricians who specialize in EV charger installation has never been higher. Shaffer Construction, Inc. has been serving the Los Angeles area, including Pasadena, with expert electrical services for years, and we have developed deep expertise in the installation of both residential and commercial EV charging infrastructure.

The unique electrical demands of EV chargers require more than basic electrical knowledge. From navigating California's Title 24 building codes to performing detailed electrical load studies and upgrading older electrical panels, proper EV charger installation demands the expertise of a licensed C-10 electrical contractor. Shaffer Construction brings this expertise to every project in Pasadena, ensuring that your property is not only ready for today's electric vehicles but also prepared for the continued growth of EV adoption in the coming years.

Why Pasadena Properties Need Qualified EV Electricians

Pasadena stands out among Los Angeles-area cities for its proactive approach to electric vehicle infrastructure. According to Pasadena Water and Power, the city offers some of the most generous EV incentives in California, including up to $1,500 rebates for customers who purchase or lease electric vehicles, $600 rebates for installing Wi-Fi enabled home EV chargers, and up to $6,000 per port for commercial smart EV charger installations. These incentives make Pasadena an ideal location for EV adoption, but they also create increased demand for qualified electricians who understand the technical requirements.

At Shaffer Construction, we help Pasadena property owners navigate these incentive programs while ensuring their electrical systems meet all safety and code requirements. Installing an EV charger is not as simple as plugging in an appliance. Level 2 EV chargers, which are the standard for home and business installations, operate on 240-volt circuits and require dedicated electrical circuits with proper amperage ratings. The Alternative Fuels Data Center notes that California has mandatory building standards for EV charging infrastructure, and only licensed C-10 electricians are legally permitted to perform these installations.

Pasadena property owners who attempt DIY installations or hire unlicensed contractors risk serious safety hazards, code violations, and potentially voided warranties on expensive EV charging equipment. Shaffer Construction's licensed electricians bring the technical knowledge and legal compliance necessary to complete every installation correctly the first time, protecting both your investment and your property.

Understanding Electrical Load Studies for EV Charging

One of the most critical steps in any EV charger installation is the electrical load study. Before installing a Level 2 EV charger, which can draw 40 to 60 amps of continuous power, a qualified electrician must assess whether your existing electrical panel has sufficient capacity to handle the additional load. The National Electrical Code classifies EV chargers as continuous loads, meaning they can operate for three hours or more without interruption. According to industry guidelines, the NEC 80% rule requires that continuous loads not exceed 80% of the total circuit capacity, which is a critical safety requirement.

Shaffer Construction performs comprehensive electrical load calculations for every EV charger installation project in Pasadena. Our load studies evaluate your home's or business's total electrical demand, including square footage, major appliances, HVAC systems, and other electrical loads. We then determine whether your existing panel has adequate capacity or whether an upgrade is necessary. This thorough assessment prevents overloaded circuits, tripped breakers, and potential fire hazards that can result from improper installations.

As we discussed in our guide on planning EV charger infrastructure installation in Los Angeles, load studies are particularly important for older Pasadena properties that may have 100-amp or even 60-amp electrical panels. These older systems were never designed to handle the sustained high-amperage draw of modern EV chargers, and attempting to install a Level 2 charger without upgrading the panel can result in serious electrical problems. Shaffer Construction's detailed load studies give Pasadena property owners the information they need to make informed decisions about their electrical infrastructure.

Panel Upgrades: When They're Necessary for EV Chargers

Many older homes and commercial buildings in Pasadena were built with 100-amp or smaller electrical service panels, which were adequate for the electrical demands of previous decades but are often insufficient for today's electrical loads, especially when adding an EV charger. According to electrical industry standards, most modern homes require 200-amp service to comfortably accommodate EV charging along with other household electrical needs.

Shaffer Construction frequently performs panel upgrades for Pasadena property owners who want to install EV chargers but have inadequate electrical capacity. A typical Level 2 EV charger requires a dedicated 40 to 60-amp circuit, and when you factor in the NEC's 80% rule, a 100-amp panel simply does not leave enough headroom for safe operation when you consider all the other electrical loads in a home or business. Our electricians can upgrade your electrical panel from 100 amps to 200 amps, providing not only the capacity needed for EV charging but also room for future electrical needs.

The panel upgrade process involves more than simply swapping out the panel box. Shaffer Construction coordinates with Pasadena Water and Power to ensure proper utility connections, obtains all necessary permits from the City of Pasadena, and ensures that the upgraded system meets current California Electrical Code requirements. Our comprehensive approach to our electrical load studies and panel upgrade services means that Pasadena property owners can trust that their electrical systems are safe, compliant, and future-ready.

In some cases where a full panel upgrade is not immediately feasible, Shaffer Construction can recommend alternative solutions such as load management systems. These smart devices monitor overall household electricity usage and temporarily reduce power to the EV charger when the panel approaches 80% capacity, then restore full charging power when other appliances cycle off. This can be a cost-effective interim solution for some Pasadena properties, though a full panel upgrade often provides the best long-term value.

Residential vs Commercial EV Infrastructure in Pasadena

The requirements for residential and commercial EV charger installations in Pasadena differ significantly, and Shaffer Construction has extensive experience with both. For residential properties, the focus is typically on installing a single Level 2 charger in a garage or carport to serve the homeowner's personal vehicle. Our residential EV charger installation services include site assessments, load calculations, permit acquisition, installation, and final inspections to ensure everything is done correctly and safely.

California's CalGreen building codes have specific requirements for new residential construction. New single-family homes and townhouses with attached garages must have electrical conduit installed that is capable of supporting a Level 2 EV charger, and new multifamily housing must have 40% of parking spaces capable of supporting EV chargers with 10% of spaces actually equipped with chargers. Shaffer Construction helps Pasadena property owners and developers comply with these requirements, whether for new construction or retrofit installations.

Commercial EV infrastructure in Pasadena presents additional complexities. Businesses installing EV chargers must consider factors such as ADA accessibility requirements, the need for multiple charging stations, smart charging capabilities for load management, and potential revenue generation through paid charging services. Shaffer Construction has installed commercial EV charging systems for office buildings, retail centers, hotels, and multifamily properties throughout the Los Angeles area, including numerous projects in Pasadena.

Our commercial installations often involve more extensive electrical work, including transformer upgrades, dedicated metering for billing purposes, and integration with building management systems. We work closely with commercial property owners to design EV charging solutions that meet both current needs and allow for future expansion as EV adoption continues to grow. As outlined in our article on preparing Los Angeles buildings for the EV charging boom, forward-thinking infrastructure planning can save property owners significant money compared to piecemeal installations.

Navigating California's EV Charger Regulations

California has some of the most comprehensive and complex electrical codes in the nation, and EV charger installations must comply with multiple overlapping regulatory frameworks. Shaffer Construction's electricians stay current with all applicable codes and regulations, including the California Electrical Code, Title 24 Building Standards, CalGreen requirements, and National Electrical Code Article 625, which specifically addresses electric vehicle charging systems.

One of the most important regulatory considerations is that EV charging equipment used for commercial purposes is subject to Division of Measurement Standards oversight, and all installations must be performed by licensed C-10 electricians. Shaffer Construction holds the proper licensing and maintains comprehensive insurance coverage to protect both our team and our clients throughout every installation project in Pasadena.

Permitting is another critical aspect of regulatory compliance. While simple Level 1 chargers that plug into standard 120-volt outlets typically do not require permits, Level 2 installations operating at 240 volts absolutely do require permits from the City of Pasadena. Shaffer Construction handles all permit applications, inspections, and final approvals, ensuring that installations meet all safety requirements and pass inspection the first time. According to California's best practices for permitting EV charging stations, the permitting process is aimed primarily at assuring safety, with most delays resulting from improper installations that do not meet code or manufacturer specifications.

Shaffer Construction's experience with Pasadena's permitting process and our relationships with local building officials help streamline the approval process. We know exactly what documentation is required, what inspection checkpoints to expect, and how to ensure that every installation meets or exceeds all applicable codes and standards. This expertise saves our Pasadena clients time, reduces stress, and ensures that their EV charging infrastructure is installed correctly and safely.
